subject: Copywriting
title: Dior: The New Look in Words
description: A quick, practical guide to Dior: The New Look in Words.

hook.text: Christian Dior launched the 'New Look' in 1947.

buildup.text: Dior's language was architectural: 'sculpted waists,' 'structured shoulders,' 'flowing skirts.' Clothing was described.

discovery.text: Modern Dior copy blends French and English seamlessly: 'savoir-faire,' 'atelier,' 'maison.' French words signal.

twist.text: Using French in luxury copy is a global convention—even Japanese and Korean luxury brands add French words to suggest.

climax.text: Dior's copy legacy: fashion language should make clothes sound like art.

quiz.question: Why do luxury brands use French words in their copy?
options: French words signal Parisian prestige and authenticity
